messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a sharp p99 jump on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate around 08:12 UTC, went from ~140ms to ~900ms in a couple minutes.
kevin: yikes. Which rollup/view are you looking at? endpoint breakdown or global?
maria: endpoint breakdown, per-region. US-W is the worst, EU unchanged. I pulled the trace for a few requests and saw a lot of time in routing/quota check.
raj: routing/quota check? Did we push the new per-tenant quota enforcement last night? deploy-bot: Deploy started by @raj at 2026-03-20T07:45:03Z — canary to 10% traffic.
kevin: oh right, that change added a synchronous call to quota-service before routing to Dedicated pools for certain customer_tiers. Maybe that added tail latency under load.
oliver: can we confirm whether the p99 is from the routing hop or from downstream model runtime? Maria, do you have a sample request id?
maria: sample ids: req-8a3f, req-8a41, req-8a5d. Last one shows 720ms spent in `quota-client` calls across retries.
monica-oncall: I'm paging quota-service team to see if they saw increased RTs. @anita-prod fyi in case this affects customer dashboards.
anita-prod: seeing spike in quota-service latency correlating with the time window. There was a spike in Redis CPU from 20%->85% during the canary. Might be hot keys from canary forcing cold caches.
raj: the canary had new tenant-level keys that use tenant_id as a primary key for token buckets. If a few noisy tenants hit simultaneously, that explains hot keys. We should fallback to async quota-check for non-critical paths.
kevin: for the dashboard side — the p95 barely moved, p99 jumped. That smells like a small fraction of requests hitting long paths (retries/hot keys). We should add a histogram sample to the console showing hop-level latencies (routing, quota, runtime).
emily-devex: +1 to showing hop-level breakdown in the console by default for endpoint detail view. UX ask: we can fold it under "Latent hops" with a sparkline and sample ids.
oliver: short term mitigation — can we change the routing policy to bypass quota-sync for the canary traffic group? Or route canary to a separate pool with pre-warmed quota caches?
raj: canary traffic had routing tag `canary-v2`. We could set a rule: if tag==canary-v2 then use `quota-mode=best-effort`. I'll make a patch but need approval from product for risk.
anita-prod: for customer-facing SLAs, we can't generally relax quota checks. But for internal canaries it's acceptable.
monica-oncall: I've rolled an emergency rule to route `canary-v2` to a cold pool with local quota caches enabled — watch the dashboards.
kevin: thanks. Also we should check how percentiles are computed in the dashboard: are we aggregating per-shard histograms or sampling raw latencies? The aggregation method affects p99 sensitivity when a few shards have hot keys.
emily-devex: current backend stores per-worker histograms (1ms buckets) and merges them at query time. That merge is exact-ish but sampling at query level can hide patterns per-tenant. UX suggestion: show per-shard p99 heatmap option.
maria: after the routing diff, p99 dropped back to ~160ms in US-W within 5 minutes. I captured screenshots.
kevin: good. Action items: 1) Raj to revert or toggle quota sync for canary and open PR for best-effort mode. 2) Infra to investigate Redis hot-key mitigation (slotting/sharding) — anita. 3) Console: add hop-level breakdown and per-shard p99 heatmap toggle — emily. 4) Platform: add a rollout gating metric that flags p99 delta > 3x in any region during canary — kevin/raj.
raj: noted, I'll open PR and include a test that simulates noisy tenants.
anita-prod: infra: I'll increase Redis replicas on the quota cluster and put a small client-side jitter on retries to smooth spikes.
monica-oncall: marking incident as "mitigated" since p99 normalized. We should still post a short postmortem with root cause and follow-ups.
emily-devex: I'll add a small dashboard widget prototype for hop breakdown and wire up an A/B in the console so we can iterate.
maria: thanks all. One UX note — when p99 jumps we should show the top-3 contributing hops inline in the alert to avoid 'is it runtime or routing' back-and-forth.
kevin: agreed. We'll add that to the gating and alert templates.
deploy-bot: Rollout rule changed by @monica-oncall: `canary-v2 -> local-quota-cache` at 2026-03-20T08:21:30Z.
raj: PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1543 — toggle `quota_mode=best_effort` for canary tags, includes integration tests that simulate bursts.
monica-oncall:closing thread — if p99 flares again, please reopen.
